clue.text: New student may be given that coat

definitions.text: New student may be given that
definitions.meaning: an elementary textbook handed to a beginner learning a subject
the first layer of paint put on a surface before the top coat

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: a basic schoolbook for beginners, and the undercoat painters apply first.

clue.text: Servant goes after farm animal that's run amok

indicators.note: tells us the servant's word comes after the animal's word

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep kept on a farm
a page is a young servant or attendant

explanation.surface: A servant chases a farm animal that has broken loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave violently and wildly is to run amok, the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Like coal maybe, as material brought to surface

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the word from the bottom to the top reads it backwards

parts.note: denim is a tough cotton fabric used for jeans

explanation.surface: Coal is a material dug up and brought to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought to surface' looks like a description of mining; in a down entry it lifts DENIM upwards, so it reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is extracted from the ground by digging, so it is dug out from pits.

clue.text: Sort of course in Religious Education given to new student

parts.note: RE is the school-subject abbreviation for Religious Education
a fresher is a first-year student at a British university

explanation.surface: A new student is put on some sort of RE course.
explanation.definitionFit: A short course that updates someone's training is a well-known type of course.

clue.text: Powder in lotion or resin seen around a pit

indicators.note: turned around, so the resin's word is read backwards

parts.note: lac is a resin secreted by certain insects, used for shellac
a mine is a coal pit

explanation.surface: A lotion containing powder, or resin found near a mine pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen around' sounds like a container, but here it means turned round; 'or' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink zinc-oxide powder is the active ingredient of the soothing skin lotion used on sunburn.

clue.text: Discarded actors start to object very loudly

parts.note: the cast is the group of actors in a play

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word object is taken

parts.note: ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Actors begin to protest at the top of their voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown away or no longer wanted is described with this adjective, as in used clothing.

clue.text: Certainly not the most exciting tales

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters of tales are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: These stories are far from the most thrilling ones around.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of little is the opposite extreme from the most.

clue.text: Drug addict in sea ship

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A drug addict found aboard a ship at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for someone who injects drugs straight into a vein.

clue.text: Soldiers of Mons once coming to premature end, terribly

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters being badly jumbled
the word once stops short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers at the Battle of Mons were cut down too early, dreadfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to premature end' trims ONCE to ONC; 'terribly' then mixes MONS and ONC.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for non-commissioned officers, such as sergeants and corporals in the army.

clue.text: Male and one female by back of the depot for demonstration

parts.note: a man is a male person
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word the is taken

parts.note: a station is a railway or bus depot

explanation.surface: A man and a woman are seen behind the depot at a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one female' looks like a single person, but gives I then F.
explanation.definitionFit: A public display of a feeling or a quality is a showing of it, an outward sign.

clue.text: US city in desert with one personality

parts.note: sand is what a desert is made of
I is the Roman numeral for one
ego is a person's sense of self or personality

explanation.surface: A city in the American desert has a character all its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Californian city on the Pacific coast near Mexico.

clue.text: Fox? Has got into hospital — bother!

indicators.note: the answer is held within the words hospital and bother, running across them

explanation.surface: Someone named Fox has ended up in hospital, which is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: William Henry Fox Talbot was a Victorian pioneer of photography; the question mark marks Fox as just part of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname completing the name of the photographic pioneer whose middle name was Fox.

clue.text: What's near fire? It's hot soil

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
earth means soil

explanation.surface: Asking what lies by the fire, with the answer hot soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The floor of a fireplace, the area right in front of and under the fire.

clue.text: Dog seen around Fleet Street area journalist rescued

indicators.note: the dog's name surrounds the postcode area

parts.note: Rover is a traditional name for a dog
EC is the London postcode district (East Central) that includes Fleet Street
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist rescued a dog spotted near Fleet Street, London's old newspaper district.
explanation.definitionFit: Something retrieved or saved has been got back, a past participle like saved.

clue.text: Castle quickly established by promontory

parts.note: fast means quickly
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness place names

explanation.surface: A castle built rapidly on a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold or secure fortified place, like a castle, an old literary word.

clue.text: Evil girl and one almost good in musical event

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing, evil
gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: the word one loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A wicked girl and a nearly good one perform at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal gathering where everybody joins in the songs together.

clue.text: Got reminder about remedial treatment

indicators.note: the reminder word goes about the treatment word

parts.note: a prod is a nudge or reminder
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: Someone received a reminder about their medical treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or acquire something, often with effort, is the same as to get it.

clue.text: Artist having item of furniture that can be valued

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: An artist owns a piece of furniture that could be appraised.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to be assessed or valued, especially property for local rates.

clue.text: The infernal world has possession of rejects

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for the underworld itself
owns means holds as property

explanation.surface: The underworld takes ownership of cast-offs.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate or cut off a connection with someone, as a parent cutting off a child.

clue.text: A bishop in the present time seen as bigoted

indicators.note: the letters go inside the present-time word

parts.note: now means the present time
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A modern bishop is regarded as prejudiced.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-minded people are intolerant, which is what bigoted means.

clue.text: Two terms of cricket go on too long

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
a run is a unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: Two cricket words for a match that lasts too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed the allotted time, as a meeting does.

clue.text: Verses of song in bars

definitions.meaning: a stave is a verse or stanza of a poem or song
wooden or metal rods or poles

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: stanzas of verse, and sticks or rods.

clue.text: Horse let out after first hint of sunshine

indicators.note: the rented word comes after the sunshine letter
only the opening letter of sunshine is taken

parts.note: to hire out is to let something out for money

explanation.surface: A horse is turned out after the first sign of sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A large heavy draught horse, an English breed.

clue.text: Attempts to get worker joining in songs

indicators.note: the worker goes inside the word for attempts

parts.note: shies are throws or attempts, as at a coconut shy
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A worker tries to join in the singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors' work songs sung while hauling ropes.

clue.text: Miss maybe in hat crossing end of street

indicators.note: the hat word goes across the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: only the last letter of street is taken

explanation.surface: A woman in a hat crosses at the end of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is an example of a form of address, like Mr or Mrs.

clue.text: English gentleman — bow-tie sort 'ere possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A dapper Englishman in a bow tie, said in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The comic upper-class hero of P. G. Wodehouse's stories, an idle English gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: P. G. Wodehouse's idle upper-class hero is the archetypal English gentleman of comic fiction.

clue.text: Taunt directed at saints is uncalled for

parts.note: to needle is to provoke or taunt

explanation.surface: Jibes aimed at holy people are unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnecessary things are not required, so they are uncalled for.

clue.text: Author without much experience, we hear

indicators.note: signals the word is said aloud

parts.note: green means inexperienced, a novice

explanation.surface: An inexperienced writer, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene was an English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene is the novelist who wrote Brighton Rock.
